calls.summary:
# MEDDICC Analysis: BlaBlaCar & GrowthBook Call

Call on [date not specified] with James Shannon (GrowthBook), Rémy Marin, Adrien Loison (BlaBlaCar CTO), and Jean Favre (BlaBlaCar).

## Attendees & Titles
- **James Shannon** – GrowthBook (vendor)
- **Rémy Marin** – BlaBlaCar (attendee, title unclear)
- **Adrien Loison** – BlaBlaCar CTO
- **Jean Favre** – BlaBlaCar (appears to have procurement/budget authority involvement)

## Quantifiable Outcomes & Metrics
The initial proposal was **$75,000 per year** for GrowthBook's starter tier, which includes 60 experiments annually, unlimited users, unlimited traffic, and unlimited events. GrowthBook proposed increasing experiments to 100 per year at the same cost as an incentive. BlaBlaCar intended to onboard **multiple development teams** with an estimated **15 teams** running experiments, though the team acknowledged difficulty estimating actual experiment volume given engineering resource constraints.

## Budget Authority Signals
Jean Favre identified significant budget constraints and authority issues. The finance team was "not very happy" with opening a new budget line before year-end, indicating reluctance around 2026 spending. The CTO expressed "mixed feelings" about the $75,000 proposal. Jean Favre possessed negotiation authority and internal alignment responsibility, serving as the bridge between technical and financial stakeholders.

## Technical Requirements
The primary technical consideration involved experiment capacity planning. Adrien Loison emphasized that experiment volume estimation was "the trickiest aspect" because running experiments required engineering resources. The uncertainty around whether 60 or 100 annual experiments would suffice reflected their immature experimentation practice rather than defined technical specifications.

## Decision Process & Timeline
A POC kickoff was scheduled for the following Tuesday. GrowthBook proposed signing by **October 28-29, 2026** with contract commencement on October 28 and first payment delayed until January 1, 2027. This structure addressed the finance team's resistance to 2026 spending. The team needed to accommodate "next quarter roadmaps" when onboarding development teams, indicating Q4 2026/Q1 2027 as the implementation window.

## Specific Pain Points
- Budget cycle misalignment between vendor and buyer year-end timelines
- Finance team resistance to new budget line items in 2026
- Uncertainty about experiment volume requirements
- Engineering resource constraints limiting experimentation velocity
- Internal legal approval requirements for case studies or brand usage

## Champion Signals
Jean Favre demonstrated strong champion behavior, actively problem-solving payment structure obstacles and seeking "alignment" to enable signing. Adrien Loison engaged constructively despite reservations, asking clarifying questions about experiment requirements. Both showed willingness to explore multi-year agreements and alternative deal structures.

## Competitors Mentioned
A competitor named **Confidence** was referenced, with GrowthBook noting their pricing was "quite low" and suggesting lower maturity in product and support compared to GrowthBook. This competitive comparison influenced BlaBlaCar's perception that $75,000 was "too high."

## Next Steps
GrowthBook committed to proposing the enhanced starter tier (100 experiments for $75,000). Discussions remained open on: cost reduction, quarterly payment splitting, multi-year agreement terms, and a joint case study or publication. BlaBlaCar needed

# Bla Bla Car & GrowthBook Commercials
Date: 2026-10-07 | Duration: 43m

## Summary
The discussion clarified that the event forwarder is optional and costs US$30 per 1 million forwarded events, while most customers use existing pipelines. The shift from a fixed US$60,000 annual fee to usage-based pricing raised budget concerns, prompting requests for scenarios covering 100, 150, and 200 experiments, overage details, and tier comparisons. James explained that higher tiers reduce overage fees, with a 143-experiment break-even point, and recommended starting at 100 experiments. Frontend exposure events occur once per user per experiment, but backend multi-instance setups may create duplicates requiring investigation. The PoC will involve two teams running live production A/B tests to assess integration, user experience, and data workflows, with onboarding support and BigQuery cost-reduction options. Legal review is planned for early the following week, with an October 28 decision target and a Tuesday afternoon follow-up.

## Keywords
event forwarder, pricing tiers, proof-of-concept, POC, experiment volume, BigQuery cost, contract review

## Action Items

**James Shannon**
Provide detailed pricing scenarios for 100, 150, and 200 experiments tiers to support internal budgeting and supplier comparison (14:44)
Verify and clarify whether stopped experiments and guardrail metrics are included or excluded from experiment counts under the contract terms (18:00)
Deliver BigQuery usage cost estimates along with optimization strategies such as pipeline mode and query improvements (25:05)
Arrange a follow-up technical support call or provide a video recording to assist with data integration and setup questions (27:22)
Follow up on backend event exposure multiple counts question raised by Adrien regarding multiple service instances sending events per user (29:39)
Enable the event forwarder feature for the PoC with appropriate cost controls and communicate the conditions to the team (30:11)
Block calendar for Tuesday 2:00 PM meeting to review contract progress and address any further questions with all participants (31:50)

**Alexandre Laigné**
Evaluate the optional usage of the event forwarder feature internally and decide whether to include it in the PoC or future plans (13:38)
Compare GrowthBook's pricing and offerings with other suppliers such as Spotify to inform procurement decisions (16:10)
Conduct internal budget and volume estimations to decide on the appropriate pricing tier and experiment count ranges for contract negotiations (20:04)
Coordinate contract review timeline aiming to start negotiations early next week and finalize before the October 28 deadline (28:33)
Confirm availability for the Tuesday 2:00 PM meeting to review contract progress and discuss further questions (32:15)

**Adrien Loison**
Assess backend implementation event tracking behavior to identify if multiple service instances cause multiple exposure events per user and report findings (08:06)
Provide the number of team members for enterprise license trial provisioning to GrowthBook (23:00)
Decide on using the event forwarder for the PoC to potentially speed up testing and notify GrowthBook accordingly (31:13)
Participate in the follow-up technical discussion or video session regarding data setup and integration questions (27:09)
Confirm availability for the Tuesday 2:00 PM meeting to review contract progress and discuss further questions (32:12)

**Jean-Baptiste Favre**
Participate in the Tuesday 2:00 or 3:00 PM meeting to review contract progress and next steps (32:30)

# Bla Bla Car & GrowthBook Commercials
Date: 2026-10-13 | Duration: 12.960000038146973m

## Summary
The discussion centered on enabling a Proof of Concept comparing Growth Book with Confidence. Alexandre Laigné proposed committing to 200 experiments annually at a capped budget of 65,000 euros per year over two years, while requesting pricing flexibility before the POC because Confidence offers a better rate. James Shannon said signing by October 28 could allow a more competitive proposal and agreed to review internal pricing models, while Alexandre requested contract review as early as October 20. The two-week trial will assess platform capabilities, planned experiment execution, usability, and stability, with James offering technical and solution support. Legal review covers the order form, DPA, and customer agreement; CEO Nicolas Brusson is the designated signer. A case study discount remains under legal review. The parties will coordinate internal approvals, resolve contract red lines, review progress in a follow-up meeting, and work toward the October 28 signing target.

## Keywords
POC, budget negotiation, contract signing, legal review, pricing proposal, case study

## Action Items

**James Shannon**
Provide a revised pricing proposal aiming to meet Bla Bla Car’s budget of €65,000 for 200 experiments, contingent on signing by October 28th (02:32)
Support Bla Bla Car technically and solution-wise to enable adequate product trial during the next two weeks (07:59)
Send updated proposals and contract documents to Bla Bla Car via email for internal review before next meeting (11:29)
Schedule a follow-up meeting early next week to discuss progress and potential next steps (11:29)

**Adrien Loison**
Ensure internal contract and data privacy reviews continue and that legal questions are addressed promptly (09:06)
Coordinate Bla Bla Car’s testing and evaluation of the GrowthBook product during the coming two weeks (08:24)

**Alexandre Laigné**
Confirm feasibility internally to meet the budget and timing constraints, aim to provide feedback by October 20th if earlier review of proposals is needed (05:13)

**Jean-Baptiste Favre**
Liaise with Bla Bla Car’s legal team to expedite contract review and to communicate urgency on case study approval (07:00)

# Bla Bla Car & GrowthBook Commercial Check In
Date: 2026-10-20 | Duration: 21.950000762939453m

## Summary
Testing stopped after conversion rates declined, while full-flow integration and Adrien LOISON’s analysis remained incomplete. The contract process advanced through Jean Baptiste, but finance validation, legal review, and documentation requirements were still pending. James Shannon must update pricing to 70,000, replace the existing 60,000 or 65,000 for 100 references, and send the full contract for review, with signature targeted around the 28th. The event forwarder was rejected for long-term use because it was considered too expensive, while a Java SDK issue was fixed within 24 hours. Java SDK updates remain slower because the external support owner is on maternity leave for another two months. SLA coverage for support responsiveness must be confirmed. French consent requirements for front-end tracking remain under review, although exposure events can be configured to send only after consent and remote evaluation is available. A follow-up is planned for Friday and may move to Monday or be cancelled if no legal update is available.

## Keywords
SDK support, Contract negotiation, Enterprise SLAs, Event forwarder, A/B testing, EU consent

- Send updated contract/order form (06:17)

- Provide consent guidance (16:47)
